entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Nechtan nepos Uerb, grandson of Uerb, was king of the Picts from 595 to around 616, and may be the same person as the Neithon son of Guipno who ruled the kingdom of Altclut. 

Born into a Pictish family of noble descent, Nechtan's early life and upbringing are shrouded in mystery. His ascension to the throne is believed to have occurred around 595 CE, following the death of his predecessor, possibly his own father. 

During his reign, Nechtan oversaw the expansion of the Pictish kingdom, which spanned parts of modern-day Scotland and northern England. He also launched a series of military campaigns against the neighboring kingdoms of Dalriada and Strathclyde, securing key victories and cementing his reputation as a formidable leader. 

Nechtan's legacy extends beyond his military conquests, as he also played a significant role in promoting the spread of Christianity throughout the Pictish kingdom. He is said to have converted to Christianity and established several monasteries, which would go on to become centers of learning and culture. 

Despite his significant contributions to Pictish history, Nechtan's life and reign remain somewhat of a mystery. He died around 616 CE, and his exact burial site remains unknown. 

"The Picts were a nation of great warriors and wise men, whose legacy continues to inspire and captivate us today," said Dr. [Historian's Name], a leading expert on Pictish history. "Nechtan nepos Uerb was a pivotal figure in this legacy, whose military campaigns and religious reforms helped shape the course of Scottish and northern English history."
